tldr: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reached hosted APIs and AMD benchmarks by Oct 14, and OrcaRouter priced it against rival models on Oct 16. The Flash-1017 update followed Oct 17-19 with stronger coding, cheaper inference and a public search API, and an independent risk paper appeared Oct 26.
whats_new: Rival.io launched GraphX on Oct 29, claiming to run DeepSeek V4 Flash on just eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs, a self-hosting cost claim the coverage does not yet back with benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Flash is now cheaper per task, has an independent safety evaluation, and has a vendor claiming a small-GPU serving footprint. Hosting cost and risk posture can both be weighed, though the footprint claim is unverified.

status.detail: Flash-1017 is out; a safety paper and a low-GPU serving claim are the newest evidence.

beats.headline: V4.1 Flash reaches inference providers and AMD benchmarks
OrcaRouter prices Flash against Nemotron 3.5 and Step 5 Preview
Flash-1017 ships with stronger coding, cheaper inference and a search API
beats.summary: Harness v0.2.1-rc1 surfaced the same day with an unannounced snapshot.

beats.headline: Roundup places Flash-1017 among open releases; a third-party paper evaluates its safety risks
Rival.io's GraphX claims Flash serving on eight L4 GPUs

open_questions: Do independent evals confirm Flash-1017's agentic gains over larger rivals?
Is the new search API priced and rate-limited for production use?
Is the unannounced snapshot a separate model or the same Flash-1017?
What do the paper's loss-of-control and manipulation findings say about Flash-1017 under agentic use?
Does GraphX publish throughput and latency numbers for Flash on eight L4 GPUs?
take_for_builders: Rerun your agent eval and cost-per-task numbers on Flash-1017 before switching, read the Oct 26 risk evaluation before granting tool access, and wait for GraphX throughput data before sizing any L4 deployment.
